A_축정합_외부주장_원문.주장: "The label is sung aloud" — caused by the cue being too verbose or too lyrical. Remedy: keep bracket cues short.
'Avoid tag stuffing. A long bracket inventory makes the map harder to read.' Recommends testing one variable at a time; 'Every retry is unrelated' results from changing too many variables at once.

'Tags being sung as lyrics' occurs when tags aren't on their own line; 'Song ignores structure tags' happens with complex tag descriptions; 'Parenthetical directions being sung' results from full sentences in parentheses.

Long bracket cues degrade: 'The model's tokenizer front-loads processing and prefers short, recognizable descriptors. Long bracketed sentences like [Ethereal synth build with rising tension over sparse percussion] get compressed into noise.' Keep each tag to 1-3 words.

Tier ranking (from a claimed 400+ generation test): gender, delivery mode (whisper, rap, belt, spoken word), BPM and basic texture (raspy, breathy) are Tier-1 reliably honored; [Whispered] is '>80% compliance'; [Spoken Word] is 'Tier 1 and one of the cleanest-complying tags Suno has'. [Falsetto] ~60%. [Intro] 'notoriously skipped entirely'.

Guidance runs AGAINST catch-all rule blocks: 'Best practice is to shorten the bracket, remove sentence-like wording and place one concise cue directly before the intended event.' Evidence favors specific targeted tags over broad instruction containers.

Countervailing caution on long bracket text: 'Use the tag as a header, then write clean lyric lines underneath it, rather than putting full lyric lines inside brackets, which can cause Suno to sing command text.' Directly at odds with the multi-line [PERFORMANCE RULES] bullet-block form.
